# Purpose

Award credit for a defensible lower-segment section cut, correct internal resultants, explicit moment and stress sign conventions, correct rectangular-section properties, valid axial-plus-bending superposition, recognition that transverse shear vanishes at the side surfaces, and an appropriately limited engineering assessment.

# Scope of the Base Problem

The base model assumes static concentrated forces, a prismatic rectangular section at a-a, small deformation, and linear-elastic nominal-stress formulas. It excludes local bend stress concentration, lower-pin contact and hole stresses, upper bolt-group behavior, connector deformation, self-weight, fatigue, impact, and nonlinear contact. The upper offset e describes the complete bracket geometry but does not enter equilibrium of the isolated lower segment.

# Supplemental Assessment Structure

- context interpretation and load path: 20%;
- student section-cut idealization and assumptions: 20%;
- internal resultants and sign convention: 20%;
- section properties and stress calculations: 30%;
- stress elements, critical point, and limitations: 10%.
